title: Lombardia's Fuel Prices: Diesel Pulls Ahead of the National Average
dek: Self-service diesel in Italy's most populous region has climbed for seven straight tracked days and now costs more than the national average.
body: Lombardia's self-service Benzina is priced at €2.069 per liter as of September 8, essentially matching Italy's national self-service average of €2.070. Gasolio tells a different story: at €2.200 per liter, self-service diesel in the region runs about 2.3 cents above the €2.198 national average — a gap wide enough to notice at the pump, and one that puts Lombardia's drivers slightly out of step with the rest of the country.

The climb has been steady rather than sudden. Over the last seven tracked days, Lombardia's self-service Benzina rose from €2.0264 to €2.0694 (+2.1%), while Gasolio moved from €2.1607 to €2.2002 (+1.8%), with the sharpest gains arriving in the final days of the stretch. Meanwhile the region's station network stayed active: 3,118 stations remain registered, and 2,835 reported fresh prices on September 8, up slightly from 2,831 the day before — a small but real sign that the reporting network keeps pace even as prices move.

Tracking one region this closely, every single day, would be a losing battle for a manually maintained spreadsheet. Fuel Dashboard covers all 20 Italian regions this way because the whole pipeline — data pull, regional rotation, and today's article — rebuilds itself automatically each morning, built with Claude Code instead of hand-updated Excel.

Today's Fuel Dashboard spotlight: Lombardia, where self-service diesel has climbed for seven straight tracked days and now costs about 2.3 cents more per liter than the Italian average.

Fuel Dashboard is a self-updating site that tracks Italy's fuel prices region by region, every day, using the official MIMIT data feed. No spreadsheet, no manual copy-paste — the whole pipeline pulls fresh data, picks a region to spotlight, and writes the day's article automatically. Take a look: https://adeo-blip.github.io/fuel-price-italy/

This is the kind of project that makes the case for building with AI tools rather than maintaining another Excel file: Claude Code wrote and now runs the data pipeline, the regional rotation logic, and the article generation, so the dashboard stays current with zero manual upkeep. It's a small example of what's possible when you let an AI coding agent own the boring, repetitive parts of a data project.
